summary: Landing and six-case library load successfully, but authenticated case start is blocked by a backend authorization-header defect.

critical.issue: Returns 401 Please sign in to continue after successful registration and sending Authorization: Bearer token.
Uses the same current_user dependency and will reject authenticated requests for the same reason.

integration_issues.issue: The failed 401 is uncaught in Library.start, producing the React runtime error overlay instead of an in-app error state.

action_items: Declare authorization parameters as Header() (or use a dependency that reads the request header) for current_user consumers, then retest sessions and progress.
Add frontend error handling around case start and chat requests so API failures do not invoke the runtime overlay.
critical_code_review_comments: current_user accepts authorization as a plain function parameter, so FastAPI treats it as a query parameter rather than the Authorization header; every protected flow is effectively unusable.
Session.send has a finally but no catch/error state, and Library.start has no catch; integration failures are exposed as uncaught runtime errors.
seed_data_creation: Created temporary TEST_ prefixed accounts during API/browser registration; no seeded production data modified.
test_credentials: No credentials were present in /app/memory/test_credentials.md; temporary account generated during testing.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Landing page and /library render with six cards. Registration succeeds. Retest authenticated starts for all six case IDs, chat/LLM response, completion score, XP persistence, progress, and mobile overflow after auth fix.
rca of the issue: In backend/server.py, current_user defines authorization: Optional[str] = Header(default=None), but protected route functions define authorization: Optional[str] = None and call current_user(authorization). FastAPI therefore does not inject the HTTP Authorization header into those route parameters, yielding None and a deterministic 401.
